official.description_text:
Researcher in Computational Spatial Biology
Apply for position
School of Engineering Sciences in Chemistry, Biotechnology and Helth at KTH
Job description
We are seeking a researcher to join the Lundeberg research group at the Department of Gene Technology, KTH. The position focuses on developing bioinformatic methods for the analysis of spatial molecular data and three-dimensional (3D) tissue reconstruction, with particular emphasis on image analysis, machine learning and computational pathology.
You will independently develop, implement and evaluate methods for integrating tissue images with spatial molecular data. The work includes analysis of large-scale imaging and omics datasets and biological interpretation of the results.
The work will be carried out in close collaboration with experimental and clinical researchers. The research group is international, and English is normally used for scientific communication.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree, or an equivalent foreign degree, in bioinformatics, computational biology, computer science, biotechnology or another relevant field, as well as documented research expertise relevant to the position.
Documented experience in the analysis of tissue images and spatial molecular data, as well as experience with GPU-based analysis.
Ability to independently develop, implement and evaluate analytical methods and analyse large-scale biological data.
Ability to independently conduct research and method development, communicate research, and contribute to the utilisation of research results.
As a person, you are proactive, self-driven and structured, with good collaborative skills.
You should also have an awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with particular focus on gender equality.
Preferred qualifications
Education or documented experience in machine learning, image analysis, spatial omics, computational pathology or related quantitative methods is advantageous.
Experience in one or more of the following areas is considered advantageous: 3D reconstruction, image registration, machine learning or deep learning, multimodal data integration, foundation models in pathology, Python programming, and working in HPC environments.
Teaching experience and experience in leading research activities or teams are considered advantageous.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system in order to apply for this position. You are responsible to ensure that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Max two pages long.
Your complete application must be received by KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The employment is valid for a limited time according to the agreement - for up to 12 months, with access according to agreement.

ai.summary: A limited-term (≤12 months) research position in computational methods for spatial molecular biology, focusing on image analysis, machine learning, and 3D tissue reconstruction. Work bridges bioinformatics, computational pathology, and large-scale imaging/omics data analysis in a KTH biotech research group.

thematic_fit.rationale: Limited thematic connection. The researcher's work centres on spatial cognition, spatial learning, and wayfinding in immersive systems—i.e., human spatial understanding in interactive environments. This position addresses spatial reconstruction and analysis of tissue at microscopic scale—a completely different domain (computational pathology, structural biology). Both concern 'spatial' phenomena, but the contexts, scales, and goals are unrelated. Not thematically aligned.

methodological_fit.rationale: Moderate methodological overlap exists. Both involve image analysis, 3D spatial data, and computational methods. The researcher has intermediate quantitative research skills and academic experience with experimental design and validation. This role emphasizes image analysis, machine learning, 3D reconstruction, and GPU-based analysis—methods adjacent to but not overlapping with the researcher's current skillset. The researcher would need to develop deep learning and GPU computing competency, but the foundational analytical thinking is present.

growth_value.rationale: This position would build skills in machine learning, image analysis, 3D reconstruction, and GPU computing—legitimate research capabilities with some portability. However, these advances are tangential to the researcher's core growth areas (collaborative immersive systems, spatial cognition research, human-centred design methodology). The position does not close stated capability gaps in HCI, experimental design for immersive systems, or multiuser interaction research. Moderate utility for general research maturation.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is prestigious and in a priority country (Sweden). The Department of Gene Technology is part of a leading biotech ecosystem. However, computational spatial biology is orthogonal to the researcher's target identity and target research communities (HCI, immersive systems). A publication in computational pathology would not strengthen candidacy for HCI/immersive systems PhD or postdoc roles. Limited strategic value for reaching target institutions (Aalto, TU Delft HCI groups). The position offers skill development but not strategic positioning.

eligibility_flags: Requires PhD or equivalent in bioinformatics, computational biology, computer science, biotechnology or related field; researcher holds MSc by Research in Creative Multimedia—disciplinary fit is ambiguous, may require explicit justification
Posting emphasizes 'tissue image analysis and spatial molecular data, GPU-based analysis'—researcher has no documented experience in these areas
Preferred qualifications list deep learning, image analysis, spatial omics—none are in researcher's demonstrated skillset; selection may favour candidates with biology/bioinformatics training
risks: Disciplinary uncertainty: Creative Multimedia MSc may not be recognized as equivalent to bioinformatics/computational biology training; hiring panel may require clarification or prioritize discipline-trained candidates
Steep learning curve: Deep learning, GPU computing, image registration, and spatial omics are new domains; ramp-up time could be significant
Limited strategic value: Domain is computational pathology/structural biology, not HCI or immersive systems. Publications and expertise here do not strengthen candidacy for future HCI roles
Temporary role: Position is limited to 12 months maximum; insufficient time to establish research identity in a new domain before returning to HCI job market
Domain isolation: KTH Department of Gene Technology is not part of HCI or immersive systems research communities; minimal networking benefit
